topic: The Physics of Pi: Colliding Blocks and Conservation Laws

sections.title: The Counter-Intuitive Hook
lecture_lines: Two blocks collide on a frictionless surface.
Tiny block m approaches massive block M.
M is one hundred to the n times m.
They bounce off a wall to calculate pi.
animations: Fade in text: Two blocks on frictionless surface. Color #FFFFFF.
Animate tiny block m approaching block M. Color #FF0000.
Fade in symbol for pi calculation. Color #FFFF00.

sections.title: Prerequisite Physics: Conservation Laws
lecture_lines: Elastic collisions conserve both momentum and energy.
Momentum balance: mv_i equals mv_f plus Mv_f.
Kinetic energy conservation: half mv squared constant.
animations: Display elastic collision energy/momentum conservation. Color #FFFFFF.

sections.title: Mapping Collisions to Phase Space
lecture_lines: Track velocities as coordinates on phase space.
The collision path traces a circular arc.
Boundary walls force the path to reflect.
animations: Show phase space with velocity coordinates. Color #FFFFFF.
Draw circular arc for collision path. Color #00FF00.
Highlight reflection off boundary walls. Color #FFFF00.

sections.title: The Geometric Connection
lecture_lines: Collisions relate to circular arc length.
Arc length maps to the ratio pi.
More mass yields more pi digits.
animations: Connect arc length to geometry. Color #FFFFFF.
Show mapping arc to pi ratio. Color #00FF00.
Illustrate increasing pi digits with mass. Color #FFFF00.

sections.title: Conclusion and Intuition Check
lecture_lines: Physical events map to continuous geometric constants.
Pi emerges from symmetry and conservation.
Mechanics and math are deeply connected.

Show pi emergence from symmetry. Color #00FF00.
